subject.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups

question: Should canonical Firecrawl and Brave plugin configuration reject prototype-inherited plugin entries and nested credential/config fields, matching the rule applied to legacy and core runtime paths?
rationale: Completing the security invariant intentionally changes compatibility for programmatically constructed plugin configuration, so the permanent owner boundary needs explicit approval rather than an inconsistent partial hardening.

options.title: Complete the boundary
options.body: Require own properties throughout canonical plugin traversal and nested fields, with focused inherited-versus-own regression coverage.

options.title: Narrow the hardening scope
options.body: Preserve inherited canonical behavior with explicit owner approval and limit the PR’s security guarantee to the specific legacy and core lookups changed.

recommendation.title: Complete the boundary
recommendation.body: Require own properties throughout canonical plugin traversal and nested fields, with focused inherited-versus-own regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their extension ownership refactor is the strongest provenance for the canonical plugin configuration contract that needs a decision.
